experiments/factory/PLAN.md. All rules in MUSE_SPEC.md "Rules" apply (no network, no Modal runs, no model calls, no

frozen files).

  `factory_version` field in teacher.py's calls).

- **§5** the cached_tokens fix in experiments/freecad/runner_fc.py.

§3 (runner_final.py), §3b (BX finisher), §6 (deploy/modal_forge.py, run_final_session.sh), §7 (compare.py). They
come in round 2.

- `~/projects/forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q experiments/final experiments/factory experiments/freecad
  experiments/train experiments/common` passes (the old 150 plus the new tests).
- `~/projects/forge/.venv/bin/python experiments/factory/make_jobs.py` writes experiments/factory/jobs.jsonl

  no network.
- `forge_train.py smoke --cap-dollars 2.0` still prints CAP REFUSED and exits 2.

- `patterns.py --runs <a folder with a fake calls.jsonl from the tests> --out X` writes patterns.md.

Report at the end: files changed, the pytest line, the self-check table, and anything you did not follow.

1|# Spec for Muse Code: factory (practice-job generator + teacher runner) — DRAFT, needs verifier + user yes
2|
3|Rules: work in ~/projects/forge; new files only in experiments/factory/; never open blind/ folders,
4|experiments/option-a/, or expected*.json contents; no network, no model calls, no commit, never print keys; reuse
5|experiments/first-test/checks.py (TOL_DIFF = 1e-6) and runner.run_code with experiments/b2-hint/sandbox_cq.sb.
6|
7|## 1. `generator.py`: deterministic practice jobs (seed 20261029)
8|Ten NEW hard-style families (each job = 4-8 features placed by exact relations; numbers vary per job within safe
9|ranges; every job's text gives every coordinate, like experiments/first-test/jobs.py texts):
10|1. Spool / bobbin: two flanges, a core, a wire slot through one flange, a centre bore.
11|2. Manifold block: a block with 2-3 cross-drilled ports along X and Y at given heights, one blind port from the top.
12|3. Dovetail slide: a block with a dovetail groove along X (given angle and widths) and two end holes. (replaces the polar
13|   flange plate: too close to exam M6, verifier A3)
14|4. Cam plate: a disk with an eccentric bore and a keyless slot at a given angle.
15|5. Pipe tee fitting: a main tube along X with a branch tube along Y, both bored through, a flange at one end.
16|   (replaces the battery holder: grid pockets too close to exam H15, verifier A3; recommended to the user)
17|6. Triangular lattice panel: a plate with a row of alternating triangular cut-outs and a solid border. (replaces the
18|   comb/fork: too close to exams H9/H4, verifier A3)
19|7. T-slot rail: a bar with a T-shaped slot along its length and end holes.
20|8. Bezel frame: a frame with a rounded-rectangle window and four mounting tabs with holes.
21|9. Ported cap: a cylinder cap with a side port (horizontal cylinder) and a top recess.
22|10. Funnel / hopper: a cone frustum shell with a cylindrical spout and a top rim. (replaces the stepped rail: too close
23|   to exam H11, verifier A3; recommended to the user)
24|Family → nearest exam job (checked by Claude from experiments/first-test/jobs-list.md; why it matters: a near-copy lets
25|the trained model memorise exam answers and makes the final exam invalid):
26|| Family | Nearest exam job | Distance |
27||---|---|---|
28|| 1 spool | M5 stepped shaft (cylinders on one axis) | different: flanges, slot through a flange |
29|| 2 manifold | H6 bearing housing (block + bores) | different: orthogonal ports at set heights |
30|| 3 dovetail | M2 T-profile (extruded profile) | different: cut groove with an angle |
31|| 4 cam plate | M12 pulley / M6 flange (disk + bore) | different: eccentric bore, angled slot |
32|| 5 pipe tee | H10 pipe clamp | different: two crossing bored tubes |
33|| 6 lattice | H15 vented lid (pattern of cut-outs) | different: triangles, alternating orientation |
34|| 7 T-slot | M7 U-channel | different: T-shaped undercut slot |
35|| 8 bezel | H2 board plate | different: rounded window, outside tabs |
36|| 9 ported cap | M3 open box / H1 enclosure | different: cylindrical, side port |
37|| 10 funnel | none close (no cones in the exam) | different |
38|Parameter ranges: every family defines min/max for each number so that features never touch or overlap by accident
39|(if they did, references could be invalid solids and teacher FAILs would measure our bug, not the teacher).
40|Each family: a function params → (text, reference_program_source); 20 jobs per family (200), ids F<family>-<n>.
41|`make_jobs.py` writes experiments/factory/jobs.jsonl (id, family, text, reference source) and a seed-chosen dev split
42|(2 per family = 20 dev ids) into split.json. Self-check: every reference builds one valid solid in-process; two
43|"wrong" variants per family (a moved feature, a wrong size) FAIL at 1e-6; print a 10-family table.
44|Overlap self-check: no job text has difflib ratio ≥ 0.9 (exact numbers) to any first-test job text (read texts from
45|experiments/first-test/jobs.py).
46|
47|## 2. `teacher.py`: Spark Open on Baseten
48|CLI: `teacher.py --jobs jobs.jsonl --ids pilot|train|all --out <dir> --budget-dollars X [--k 1] [--retry-failed]`.
49|Prompt = system "You write CadQuery Python code. Units are millimetres. Assign the final solid to a variable named result.
50|Reply with exactly one Python code block and nothing else." + user "Here is the CadQuery manual. Use it.\n\n" + manual
51|+ "\n\n" + job text. Body: model meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026, max_tokens 16000, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95,
52|header x-session-affinity (same value per run, for prompt caching). Key from env BASETEN_KEY. 8 parallel workers.
53|Each answer: extract the code, run it in the sandbox, score against the job's reference at 1e-6. Log per call: id,
54|usage (incl. prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens), latency, verdict, fails. Budget guard counts cost from usage
55|($1.25/M uncached input, $0.15/M cached, $4.25/M output); the stop rule is the in-flight rule below.
56|Pilot = the 20 non-dev ids that come first per family (2 per family), never dev ids.
57|`--ids train` skips every id that already has an answer in earlier runs' calls.jsonl (pass `--prior <dirs>`), and
58|train_records.jsonl holds at most one record per id (the first PASS). Why: without this the pilot jobs get paid for
59|twice and the same job could appear twice in training (verifier A6).
60|`--escalate` (decision, user 2026-10-29): for every id Spark FAILED, ask Muse Wonder (`muse-wonder-1.0`, api.meta.ai,
61|META_HERDSHOT_API_KEY, same prompt) once; keep its answer only if it PASSES at 1e-6. Each record gets `teacher: spark|wonder`;
62|summary reports the share of records from Wonder (why: privacy reporting; Wonder is a closed API). Separate budget
63|`--budget-w` (Meta credit).
64|`--retry-failed` re-asks only FAILed ids (k = 2 at most) while the budget lasts. The budget guard stops new calls when
65|spent + 8 in-flight calls × $0.075 would pass the budget (why: in-flight answers still cost money, verifier A2).
66|Log `cached_tokens` from usage in every record (why: x-session-affinity caching is not verified; cost depends on it).
67|Output: calls.jsonl, summary.json (pass rate per family, tokens, cost), and `train_records.jsonl` = {"id","text","code"}
68|for every PASS at 1e-6 among non-dev ids (code = the teacher's extracted code).
69|
70|## 3. Tests (offline, fake HTTP)
71|Generator determinism (same seed → same file), every reference valid, wrong variants fail, overlap check, dev split
72|excluded from pilot/train records, budget guard math with cached tokens, a fake teacher reply that PASSes ends up in
73|train_records.jsonl and a FAIL does not. Run `~/projects/forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q experiments/factory`.

1|# Factory plan: hard-style practice jobs → teacher answers → strict referee → training data (DRAFT)
2|
3|Status: DRAFT by Claude, 2026-10-29. Needs: verifier check (plan + spec), the user's yes, then Muse Code builds the
4|generator and the teacher runner (spec: experiments/factory/SPEC.md). Goal link: forge-wiki/wiki/decisions/new-goal-2026-10-29.md.
5|
6|## Question
7|Can the teacher (Muse Spark Open on Baseten) produce ~150+ referee-verified solutions to **hard-style** CadQuery jobs
8|from part families that are **not** in the 30-job exam, cheaply enough to train Glimmer on?
9|
10|## Data rules (decisions)
11|- Practice families are new (list in SPEC §1); none of the exam families in experiments/first-test/jobs-list.md.
12|  The training pipeline's exam guard (FIX_SPEC item 3) re-checks every kept answer before training.
13|- Every job is generated with exact coordinates in the same text style as the exam ("X from a to b ..."), and a
14|  reference program built by the generator (deterministic, seeded). The reference is used ONLY by the referee.
15|- Strict referee: experiments/first-test/checks.py at TOL_DIFF = 1e-6 (user rule), run in the sandbox.
16|- Training records = the teacher's code (not the generator's reference), only when it PASSES at 1e-6.
17|- Split: ~180 training jobs + 20 dev jobs (seed-chosen before any teacher call; dev jobs are never trained on and are
18|  used only to pick training settings).
19|
20|## Teacher run
21|- Spark Open (`meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026`, Baseten), prompt = system message + the CadQuery manual
22|  (experiments/first-test/manual.md) + job text, max_tokens 16,000, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, k = 1, a second try
23|  (k = 2) only for jobs that failed, if money allows. The teacher may use the manual; Glimmer's training records use the
24|  short prompt (no manual).
25|- Pilot first: 20 jobs (2 per family). Gate: 0 harness errors, then the yield rule below decides the main-run size.
26|
27|## Money and caps (corrected after the verifier: WRONG output-length assumption)
28|Measured: Spark Open's answers to hard first-test jobs average **5,212 output tokens** (first-test arm C) → ≈ $0.023 per
29|call ($1.25 / $0.15 cached / $4.25 per M; output dominates). Pilot 20 ≈ $0.46; main 180 ≈ $4.2; retries extra.
30|**Cap $5 on Baseten** (Forge's $30 budget; more only if the user raises it under the "final, winnable project" rule).
31|Within $5: the guard keeps 8 × $0.075 = $0.60 for in-flight answers, so ≈ $4.40 is usable → pilot + about 170 first
32|tries (expected records ≈ 170 × p), retries only with what is left. Muse Code build ≈ $0.5-1.
33|## Yield rule (verifier A1)
34|Target ≥ 150 kept records needs a first-try pass rate p ≥ 83% (150/180). At the pilot gate: if p ≥ 0.83, run 180 jobs;
35|if 0.5 ≤ p < 0.83, either accept fewer records (expected 180 × p, e.g. ≈ 110 at 60%) or ask the user to raise the
36|cap to run ceil(150/p) jobs (max 300); if p < 0.5, stop and fix the families. Why: too few records may train too weakly;
37|too many jobs at a low pass rate burns the budget without the retry money.
38|## Blind rebuild before the pilot (verifier A4)
39|Claude rebuilds 1 job per family from its text alone (no reference) and must PASS at 1e-6 (10/10). Why: otherwise a
40|teacher FAIL could mean our wording is ambiguous, not that the teacher is wrong.
41|## Dev jobs
42|Scored with the final-exam runner and the 0.2% referee (like the exam), with 1e-6 also reported. Why: training settings
43|must be chosen with the same yardstick as the final exam.
44|
45|## Report
46|Pass rate per family (pilot and main), tokens per answer, kept records (count, token lengths: must be ≤ 4,096 with
47|the short prompt), the exam-guard report, the dev split, and cost (Baseten usage).
48|
49|## Freeze
50|SPEC, generator code + seed + generated jobs file, referee, sandbox, teacher runner, prompt — sha256 recorded here before
51|the pilot.
52|
53|## Privacy headline (decision, user 2026-10-29)
54|Headline: "a private teacher; Wonder only helps on the hardest jobs (X% of the data)", X = share of kept records
55|tagged `teacher: wonder`, printed next to the headline in the factory summary. Large X is stated openly. See
56|forge-wiki/wiki/decisions/new-goal-2026-10-29.md.

8|Ten NEW hard-style families (each job = 4-8 features placed by exact relations; numbers vary per job within safe
9|ranges; every job's text gives every coordinate, like experiments/first-test/jobs.py texts):
10|1. Spool / bobbin: two flanges, a core, a wire slot through one flange, a centre bore.
11|2. Manifold block: a block with 2-3 cross-drilled ports along X and Y at given heights, one blind port from the top.
12|3. Dovetail slide: a block with a dovetail groove along X (given angle and widths) and two end holes. (replaces the polar
13|   flange plate: too close to exam M6, verifier A3)
14|4. Cam plate: a disk with an eccentric bore and a keyless slot at a given angle.
15|5. Pipe tee fitting: a main tube along X with a branch tube along Y, both bored through, a flange at one end.
16|   (replaces the battery holder: grid pockets too close to exam H15, verifier A3; recommended to the user)
17|6. Triangular lattice panel: a plate with a row of alternating triangular cut-outs and a solid border. (replaces the
18|   comb/fork: too close to exams H9/H4, verifier A3)
19|7. T-slot rail: a bar with a T-shaped slot along its length and end holes.
20|8. Bezel frame: a frame with a rounded-rectangle window and four mounting tabs with holes.
21|9. Ported cap: a cylinder cap with a side port (horizontal cylinder) and a top recess.
22|10. Funnel / hopper: a cone frustum shell with a cylindrical spout and a top rim. (replaces the stepped rail: too close
23|   to exam H11, verifier A3; recommended to the user)
24|Family → nearest exam job (checked by Claude from experiments/first-test/jobs-list.md; why it matters: a near-copy lets
25|the trained model memorise exam answers and makes the final exam invalid):
26|| Family | Nearest exam job | Distance |
27||---|---|---|
28|| 1 spool | M5 stepped shaft (cylinders on one axis) | different: flanges, slot through a flange |
29|| 2 manifold | H6 bearing housing (block + bores) | different: orthogonal ports at set heights |
30|| 3 dovetail | M2 T-profile (extruded profile) | different: cut groove with an angle |
31|| 4 cam plate | M12 pulley / M6 flange (disk + bore) | different: eccentric bore, angled slot |
32|| 5 pipe tee | H10 pipe clamp | different: two crossing bored tubes |

34|| 7 T-slot | M7 U-channel | different: T-shaped undercut slot |
35|| 8 bezel | H2 board plate | different: rounded window, outside tabs |
36|| 9 ported cap | M3 open box / H1 enclosure | different: cylindrical, side port |

1|# Factory plan: hard-style practice jobs → teacher answers → strict referee → training data (DRAFT)
2|
3|Status: DRAFT by Claude, 2026-10-29. Needs: verifier check (plan + spec), the user's yes, then Muse Code builds the
4|generator and the teacher runner (spec: experiments/factory/SPEC.md). Goal link: forge-wiki/wiki/decisions/new-goal-2026-10-29.md.
5|
6|## Question
7|Can the teacher (Muse Spark Open on Baseten) produce ~150+ referee-verified solutions to **hard-style** CadQuery jobs
8|from part families that are **not** in the 30-job exam, cheaply enough to train Glimmer on?
9|
10|## Data rules (decisions)
11|- Practice families are new (list in SPEC §1); none of the exam families in experiments/first-test/jobs-list.md.
12|  The training pipeline's exam guard (FIX_SPEC item 3) re-checks every kept answer before training.
13|- Every job is generated with exact coordinates in the same text style as the exam ("X from a to b ..."), and a
14|  reference program built by the generator (deterministic, seeded). The reference is used ONLY by the referee.
15|- Strict referee: experiments/first-test/checks.py at TOL_DIFF = 1e-6 (user rule), run in the sandbox.
16|- Training records = the teacher's code (not the generator's reference), only when it PASSES at 1e-6.
17|- Split: ~180 training jobs + 20 dev jobs (seed-chosen before any teacher call; dev jobs are never trained on and are
18|  used only to pick training settings).
19|
20|## Teacher run
21|- Spark Open (`meta-models/muse-spark-open-1026`, Baseten), prompt = system message + the CadQuery manual
22|  (experiments/first-test/manual.md) + job text, max_tokens 16,000, temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, k = 1, a second try
23|  (k = 2) only for jobs that failed, if money allows. The teacher may use the manual; Glimmer's training records use the
24|  short prompt (no manual).
25|- Pilot first: 20 jobs (2 per family). Gate: 0 harness errors, then the yield rule below decides the main-run size.
26|
27|## Money and caps (corrected after the verifier: WRONG output-length assumption)
28|Measured: Spark Open's answers to hard first-test jobs average **5,212 output tokens** (first-test arm C) → ≈ $0.023 per
29|call ($1.25 / $0.15 cached / $4.25 per M; output dominates). Pilot 20 ≈ $0.46; main 180 ≈ $4.2; retries extra.
30|**Cap $5 on Baseten** (Forge's $30 budget; more only if the user raises it under the "final, winnable project" rule).
31|Within $5: the guard keeps 8 × $0.075 = $0.60 for in-flight answers, so ≈ $4.40 is usable → pilot + about 170 first
32|tries (expected records ≈ 170 × p), retries only with what is left. Muse Code build ≈ $0.5-1.
33|## Yield rule (verifier A1)
34|Target ≥ 150 kept records needs a first-try pass rate p ≥ 83% (150/180). At the pilot gate: if p ≥ 0.83, run 180 jobs;
35|if 0.5 ≤ p < 0.83, either accept fewer records (expected 180 × p, e.g. ≈ 110 at 60%) or ask the user to raise the
36|cap to run ceil(150/p) jobs (max 300); if p < 0.5, stop and fix the families. Why: too few records may train too weakly;
37|too many jobs at a low pass rate burns the budget without the retry money.
38|## Blind rebuild before the pilot (verifier A4)
39|Claude rebuilds 1 job per family from its text alone (no reference) and must PASS at 1e-6 (10/10). Why: otherwise a
40|teacher FAIL could mean our wording is ambiguous, not that the teacher is wrong.
41|## Dev jobs
42|Scored with the final-exam runner and the 0.2% referee (like the exam), with 1e-6 also reported. Why: training settings
43|must be chosen with the same yardstick as the final exam.
44|
45|## Report
46|Pass rate per family (pilot and main), tokens per answer, kept records (count, token lengths: must be ≤ 4,096 with
47|the short prompt), the exam-guard report, the dev split, and cost (Baseten usage).
48|
49|## Freeze
50|SPEC, generator code + seed + generated jobs file, referee, sandbox, teacher runner, prompt — sha256 recorded here before
51|the pilot.
52|
53|## Privacy headline (decision, user 2026-10-29)
54|Headline: "a private teacher; Wonder only helps on the hardest jobs (X% of the data)", X = share of kept records
55|tagged `teacher: wonder`, printed next to the headline in the factory summary. Large X is stated openly. See
56|forge-wiki/wiki/decisions/new-goal-2026-10-29.md.

1|"""Cloud grader for FreeCAD answers (SPEC section 2).
2|
3|A separate Modal Function (CPU, our own trusted code) with CadQuery 2.8
4|+ both exams baked into its image:
5|  /grader/first-test/{jobs.py, expected.json}
6|  /grader/thinking/{thinking_jobs.py, expected.json}
7|  /grader/checks.py (shared).
8|Input: job id + STEP bytes (+ exam); output: the verdict at 0.2% (the
9|verdict) and at 1e-6, the failed checks, measurements. It never runs
10|model code: the STEP is only imported and measured.
11|
12|Why: the reference parts live only here, never in the answer box.
13|
14|The reference values are loaded inside the image build / grader only
15|(load_expected); they are never printed or logged. Tests use small fake
16|expected dicts, never the real file.
17|"""
18|
19|import os
20|
21|TOL_VERDICT = 0.002  # 0.2%: the verdict (the baseline's yardstick)
22|TOL_TIGHT = 1e-6  # also recorded
23|
24|FIRST_TEST_DIR = os.path.join(
25|    os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "first-test")
26|THINKING_DIR = os.path.join(
27|    os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "thinking")
28|EXPECTED_NAME = "expected.json"
29|VALID_EXAMS = ("first-test", "thinking")
30|
31|try:
32|    import modal
33|except ImportError:  # offline: pure grading helpers still work
34|    modal = None
35|
36|
37|def expected_path(path=None):
38|    """Path of the baked-in expected.json (first-test dir by default)."""
39|    return path or os.path.join(FIRST_TEST_DIR, EXPECTED_NAME)
40|
41|
42|def load_expected(path=None):
43|    """Load expected.json (grader image build only). Never print it."""
44|    import json as _json
45|
46|    with open(expected_path(path), encoding="utf-8") as f:
47|        return _json.load(f)
48|
49|
50|def combine_verdict(check_fails, mismatch, tol):
51|    """PASS iff every check holds and the mismatch fraction is within tol.
52|
53|    `check_fails`: failed checks at the baseline yardstick (bbox, volume,
54|    ...); `mismatch`: answer-XOR-reference fraction of reference volume
55|    (None when the shape could not be intersected). Returns
56|    (passed, fails).
57|    """
58|    fails = list(check_fails or [])
59|    if mismatch is None:
60|        fails = fails + ["mismatch error"]
61|    elif mismatch > tol:
62|        fails = fails + ["mismatch %.1f%%" % (100.0 * mismatch)]
63|    return (not fails), fails
64|
65|
66|def grade_result(check_fails, mismatch, measurements):
67|    """Grade one imported STEP: verdict at 0.2% + the 1e-6 recording.
68|
69|    Returns {"verdict", "tight", "fails", "fails_tight", "measurements"}.
70|    Pure (no cadquery): the Modal function supplies check_fails and the
71|    mismatch fraction from checks.score; tests pass synthetic values.
72|    """
73|    passed, fails = combine_verdict(check_fails, mismatch, TOL_VERDICT)
74|    passed_tight, fails_tight = combine_verdict(check_fails, mismatch, TOL_TIGHT)
75|    return {
76|        "verdict": "PASS" if passed else "FAIL",
77|        "tight": "PASS" if passed_tight else "FAIL",
78|        "fails": fails,
79|        "fails_tight": fails_tight,
80|        "measurements": measurements,
81|    }
82|
83|
84|def grade_measurements(measure, expected, mismatch):
85|    """Grade from already-measured values (offline helper).
86|
87|    `measure`: {"bbox", ...} of the answer; `expected`: the job's
88|    expected values; `mismatch`: the XOR fraction. check_fails come from
89|    the baseline compare (bbox faces within 0.1 mm, volume/area within
90|    1%, com within 0.3 mm, exactly 1 valid solid).
91|    """
92|    return grade_result(compare_measurements(measure, expected), mismatch, measure)
93|
94|
95|def compare_measurements(m, e):
96|    """Baseline check failures for measured values (mirrors checks.compare)."""
97|    fails = []
98|    try:
99|        if m.get("solids") != 1:
100|            fails.append("solids=%s" % m.get("solids"))
101|        if not m.get("valid", True):
102|            fails.append("invalid shape")
103|        if any(abs(a - b) > 0.1 for a, b in zip(m["bbox"], e["bbox"])):
104|            fails.append("bbox")
105|        for k in ("volume", "area"):
106|            if k in m and k in e and abs(m[k] - e[k]) > 0.01 * abs(e[k]):
107|                fails.append(k)
108|        if "com" in m and "com" in e and any(
109|                abs(a - b) > 0.3 for a, b in zip(m["com"], e["com"])):
110|            fails.append("com")
111|    except (KeyError, TypeError):
112|        fails.append("scoring error")
113|    return fails
114|
115|
116|def build_grader_image():
117|    """Modal image for the grader function: CadQuery 2.8 + both exams
118|    baked in (references live only here). libGL etc. are apt-installed
119|    before pip: CadQuery's OCP needs libGL.so.1."""
120|    if modal is None:
121|        raise RuntimeError("modal is not installed; cannot build the grader")
122|    return (
123|        modal.Image.from_registry("python:3.12-slim")
124|        .apt_install("libgl1", "libglib2.0-0", "libxrender1", "libx11-6",
125|                     "libxext6")
126|        .pip_install("cadquery==2.8")
127|        .add_local_file(
128|            os.path.join(FIRST_TEST_DIR, "jobs.py"),
129|            "/grader/first-test/jobs.py")
130|        .add_local_file(
131|            os.path.join(FIRST_TEST_DIR, "checks.py"), "/grader/checks.py")
132|        .add_local_file(
133|            os.path.join(FIRST_TEST_DIR, EXPECTED_NAME),
134|            "/grader/first-test/expected.json")
135|        .add_local_file(
136|            os.path.join(THINKING_DIR, "thinking_jobs.py"),
137|            "/grader/thinking/thinking_jobs.py")
138|        .add_local_file(
139|            os.path.join(THINKING_DIR, EXPECTED_NAME),
140|            "/grader/thinking/expected.json")
141|    )
142|
143|
144|GRADER_APP_NAME = "forge-freecad-grader"  # Modal app the grader runs under
145|
146|
147|if modal is not None:
148|    _grader_image = None
149|
150|    def _image():
151|        global _grader_image
152|        if _grader_image is None:
153|            _grader_image = build_grader_image()
154|        return _grader_image
155|
156|    _app = modal.App(GRADER_APP_NAME)
157|
158|    @_app.function(image=_image(), cpu=1, timeout=300)
159|    def grade(job_id, step_bytes, exam="first-test"):
160|        """Grade one STEP (bytes) for one job id in one exam. The
161|        exam's folder is picked so one exam's ids never resolve
162|        against the other's jobs. Never runs model code."""
163|        import sys as _sys
164|        import tempfile as _tf
165|
166|        _sys.path.insert(0, "/grader")
167|        import checks as _checks  # noqa: E402
168|        from cadquery import importers as _importers  # noqa: E402
169|        if exam == "thinking":
170|            _sys.path.insert(0, "/grader/thinking")
171|            import thinking_jobs as _jobs  # noqa: E402
172|            expected = load_expected("/grader/thinking/expected.json")
173|        else:
174|            _sys.path.insert(0, "/grader/first-test")
175|            import jobs as _jobs  # noqa: E402
176|            expected = load_expected("/grader/first-test/expected.json")
177|        job = next(j for j in _jobs.JOBS if j["id"] == job_id)
178|        with _tf.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".step", delete=False) as f:
179|            f.write(bytes(step_bytes))
180|            path = f.name
181|        answer = _importers.importStep(path)
182|        ref = job["build"]()
183|        old = _checks.TOL_DIFF
184|        try:
185|            _checks.TOL_DIFF = TOL_VERDICT
186|            passed, fails, m = _checks.score(answer, ref, expected[job_id])
187|            d = m.get("mismatch")
188|            _checks.TOL_DIFF = TOL_TIGHT
189|            passed_t, fails_t, _m2 = _checks.score(answer, ref, expected[job_id])
190|        finally:
191|            _checks.TOL_DIFF = old
192|        return {
193|            "verdict": "PASS" if passed else "FAIL",
194|            "tight": "PASS" if passed_t else "FAIL",
195|            "fails": list(fails),
196|            "fails_tight": list(fails_t),
197|            "mismatch": d,
198|            "measurements": {k: m.get(k) for k in
199|                             ("bbox", "volume", "area", "com", "solids", "valid")},
200|        }
201|
202|
203|# ------------------------------------------------------- live check CLI
204|# (Claude runs this against real Modal; never in unit tests.)
205|
206|
207|def check_refs(build_refs_fn=None, grade_fn=None, exam="first-test"):
208|    """Send the main-exam references through the grader.
209|
210|    Prints `REFS n/total PASS` (the grader holds the references, so
211|    all must PASS: 30 for first-test, 13 for thinking).
212|    `build_refs_fn(job)` returns STEP bytes for one job and defaults
213|    to exporting the reference part locally (needs cadquery);
214|    `grade_fn(job_id, step_bytes)` defaults to the cloud grader for
215|    this exam (needs the grader app context). Both are injected in
216|    tests. Returns (n_pass, n_jobs).
217|    """
218|    import sys as _sys
219|
220|    if exam == "thinking":
221|        _sys.path.insert(0, THINKING_DIR)
222|        import thinking_jobs as _jobs  # noqa: E402  (frozen; not modified)
223|    else:
224|        _sys.path.insert(0, FIRST_TEST_DIR)
225|        import jobs as _jobs  # noqa: E402  (frozen file; imported, not modified)
226|
227|    if build_refs_fn is None:
228|        def build_refs_fn(job):
229|            import tempfile as _tf
230|
231|            from cadquery import exporters as _exporters
232|
233|            with _tf.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".step",
234|                                        delete=False) as f:
235|                path = f.name
236|            _exporters.export(job["build"](), path)
237|            with open(path, "rb") as f:
238|                return f.read()
239|
240|    if grade_fn is None:
241|        def grade_fn(job_id, step_bytes, _exam=exam):
242|            return grade.remote(job_id, step_bytes, _exam)
243|    n_pass, n_jobs = 0, 0
244|    # The main jobs (medium + hard), never selected by id: both exams
245|    # use the ids D1 and D2.
246|    for job in [j for j in _jobs.JOBS if j.get("level") != "dry"]:
247|        n_jobs += 1
248|        graded = grade_fn(job["id"], build_refs_fn(job))
249|        if graded.get("verdict") == "PASS":
250|            n_pass += 1
251|        else:
252|            print("REF FAIL %s: %s" % (job["id"], graded.get("fails")))
253|    print("REFS %d/%d PASS" % (n_pass, n_jobs))
254|    return n_pass, n_jobs
255|
256|
257|def main(argv=None):
258|    """CLI: --check-refs sends the exam's references through the grader
259|    (--exam thinking checks the 13 thinking jobs: REFS 13/13 PASS)."""
260|    import argparse as _ap
261|
262|    parser = _ap.ArgumentParser(description="FreeCAD cloud-grader checks.")
263|    parser.add_argument("--check-refs", action="store_true")
264|    parser.add_argument("--exam", choices=VALID_EXAMS, default="first-test")
265|    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
266|    if args.check_refs:
267|        if modal is None:
268|            raise RuntimeError(
269|                "modal is not installed; cannot reach the grader")
270|        # Grade inside the App that defines grade: App.lookup(...).run()
271|        # fails with "App is already running".
272|        with modal.enable_output():
273|            with _app.run():
274|                check_refs(exam=args.exam)
275|        return 0
276|    parser.error("need --check-refs")
277|    return 2
278|
279|

281|    import sys as _sys
282|
283|    _sys.exit(main())

404|def speed_cost_per_arm(records, arm):
405|    """Speed and cost per answer for one arm (Round 2 item 2).
406|
407|    Wall time is request sent to response received per answer
408|    (`t_call_s`, the model call only). Tokens are means per answer;
409|    $ per answer is the mean model-token $ (None for unmetered arms);
410|    answers per dollar is None when the cost is zero or unmetered."""
411|    recs = [r for r in records if r.get("arm") == arm]
412|    n = len(recs)
413|    times = []
414|    in_tok, cached_tok, out_tok = [], [], []
415|    costs = []
416|    for r in recs:
417|        t = _num_or_none(r.get("t_call_s", r.get("latency")))
418|        if t is not None:
419|            times.append(t)
420|        usage = r.get("usage") or {}
421|        in_tok.append(_num_or_none(usage.get("prompt_tokens")) or 0.0)
422|        cached_tok.append(float(cached_tokens_of(usage)))
423|        out_tok.append(_num_or_none(usage.get("completion_tokens")) or 0.0)
424|        if arm in ("S", "W"):

431|        "mean_input_tokens": (sum(in_tok) / n) if n else None,
432|        "mean_cached_tokens": (sum(cached_tok) / n) if n else None,
433|        "mean_output_tokens": (sum(out_tok) / n) if n else None,
434|        "cost_per_answer": ((total_cost / n) if n else None)
435|        if arm in ("S", "W") else None,

193|def plan_timeouts(cap_dollars, steps, startup_s=0, spent_dollars=0.0):
194|    """Derive each Modal function's timeout from the money left.
195|
196|    `steps` is a list of (name, rate_per_hour, want_seconds), charged in
197|    order. `startup_s` is the Modal startup allowance per function: the
198|    worst-case cost of a step is (startup_s + want) * rate, and that is
199|    what must fit in the money left. `spent_dollars` carries earlier spend
200|    in the same entrypoint run (train -> merge -> serve share one cap).
201|    Returns {name: seconds} plus `_left`. Raises CapExceeded when a step
202|    does not fit in the money left (refuses to start it).
203|    """
204|    left = float(cap_dollars) - float(spent_dollars or 0.0)
205|    out = {}
206|    for name, rate, want in steps:
207|        cost = dollars_for_seconds(startup_s + want, rate)
208|        if cost > left:
209|            raise CapExceeded(
210|                "step %r wants %ds + %ds startup ($%.2f at $%.2f/h) but only "
211|                "$%.2f is left of the $%.2f cap; refusing to start it"
212|                % (name, want, startup_s, cost, rate, left, cap_dollars)
213|            )
214|        out[name] = want
215|        left -= cost
216|    out["_left"] = round(left, 2)
217|    return out

220|def split_cap(cap_dollars, spent_dollars=0.0, startup_s=STARTUP_TIMEOUT_S):
221|    """Reserve merge + serve first, hand the rest to train.
222|
223|    Merge gets 12 min H100, serve 6 min A100; train gets whatever the cap
224|    still covers (startup included). Refuses (CapExceeded) when train
225|    would get under 15 min. Returns {train, merge, serve, startup_s}.
226|    """
227|    merge_cost = dollars_for_seconds(startup_s + MERGE_RESERVE_S, H100_RATE)
228|    serve_cost = dollars_for_seconds(startup_s + SERVE_RESERVE_S, A100_RATE)
229|    left = float(cap_dollars) - float(spent_dollars or 0.0)
230|    if merge_cost + serve_cost > left:
231|        raise CapExceeded(
232|            "cap $%.2f (spent $%.2f) cannot reserve merge $%.2f + serve "
233|            "$%.2f; refusing" % (cap_dollars, spent_dollars or 0.0,
234|                                 merge_cost, serve_cost)
235|        )
236|    train_budget = left - merge_cost - serve_cost
237|    train_s = train_budget * 3600.0 / H100_RATE - startup_s
238|    if train_s < MIN_TRAIN_S:
239|        raise CapExceeded(
240|            "cap $%.2f leaves only %ds for train (under %ds); refusing"
241|            % (cap_dollars, max(0, int(train_s)), MIN_TRAIN_S)
242|        )
243|    return {"train": int(train_s), "merge": MERGE_RESERVE_S,
244|            "serve": SERVE_RESERVE_S, "startup_s": startup_s}

257|def plan_optimizer_steps(n_examples, epochs, grad_accum, max_steps=None):
258|    """Pure schedule: MICRO-steps (one example each) vs OPTIMIZER steps.
259|
260|    Loops epochs x examples; an optimizer step fires every grad_accum
261|    micro-steps, plus once more at the end for a leftover partial group.
262|    `max_steps` caps OPTIMIZER steps. Returns {"micro_steps",
263|    "optimizer_steps", "groups"} where groups lists each optimizer step's
264|    micro-step count (the last may be a smaller partial group).
265|    """
266|    if grad_accum < 1:
267|        raise ValueError("grad_accum must be >= 1")
268|    total_micro = max(0, int(n_examples)) * max(0, int(epochs))
269|    full = total_micro // grad_accum
270|    groups = [grad_accum] * full
271|    leftover = total_micro - full * grad_accum
272|    if leftover:
273|        groups.append(leftover)
274|    if max_steps is not None:
275|        groups = groups[:max(0, int(max_steps))]
276|    return {"micro_steps": sum(groups),
277|            "optimizer_steps": len(groups),
278|            "groups": groups}

"""Measure a CadQuery result and compare it with a job's expected values (PLAN.md section 6)."""
import cadquery as cq

TOL_POS = 0.1      # mm, bounding-box faces
TOL_COM = 0.3      # mm, centre of mass
TOL_REL = 0.01     # 1 %, volume and surface area
TOL_DIFF = 0.002   # 0.2 % of the reference volume may differ (answer XOR reference); B-rep booleans are exact


def to_shape(result):
    if isinstance(result, cq.Workplane):
        vals = [v for v in result.vals() if isinstance(v, cq.Shape)]
        return vals[0] if len(vals) == 1 else cq.Compound.makeCompound(vals)
    if isinstance(result, cq.Assembly):
        return result.toCompound()
    return result


def measure(result):
    s = to_shape(result)
    bb = s.BoundingBox()
    com = cq.Shape.centerOfMass(s)
    return {
        "bbox": [round(v, 3) for v in (bb.xmin, bb.ymin, bb.zmin, bb.xmax, bb.ymax, bb.zmax)],
        "volume": round(s.Volume(), 3),
        "area": round(s.Area(), 3),
        "com": [round(com.x, 3), round(com.y, 3), round(com.z, 3)],
        "solids": len(s.Solids()),
        "valid": bool(s.isValid()),
    }


def compare(m, e):
    """Return the list of failed checks (empty list = PASS)."""
    fails = []
    if m["solids"] != 1:
        fails.append(f"solids={m['solids']}")
    if not m["valid"]:
        fails.append("invalid shape")
    if any(abs(a - b) > TOL_POS for a, b in zip(m["bbox"], e["bbox"])):
        fails.append("bbox")
    for k in ("volume", "area"):
        if abs(m[k] - e[k]) > TOL_REL * abs(e[k]):
            fails.append(k)
    if any(abs(a - b) > TOL_COM for a, b in zip(m["com"], e["com"])):
        fails.append("com")
    return fails


def mismatch(answer, reference):
    """Volume that is in one part but not the other, as a fraction of the reference volume.
    Catches any moved feature, even symmetric moves that keep size, volume, area and centre of mass."""
    a, r = to_shape(answer), to_shape(reference)
    inter = a.intersect(r).Volume()
    return (a.Volume() + r.Volume() - 2 * inter) / r.Volume()


def score(answer, reference, expected):
    """PASS if every check holds. Returns (passed, failed_checks, measurements)."""
    m = measure(answer)
    fails = compare(m, expected)
    try:
        d = mismatch(answer, reference)
    except Exception as e:  # a broken shape can't be intersected
        d, fails = None, fails + [f"mismatch error {e!r}"[:120]]
    m["mismatch"] = None if d is None else round(d, 5)
    if d is not None and d > TOL_DIFF:
        fails.append(f"mismatch {d:.1%}")
    return (not fails), fails, m

import math

    """Cylinder of radius r starting at point p, going h along direction d."""
    return Solid.makeCylinder(r, h, Vector(*p), Vector(*d))

    return cyl(r, (x, y, z0), (0, 0, 1), z1 - z0)

    """Obround slot along X: straight part (length - width) plus two round ends, total length `length`."""
    half = (length - width) / 2
    s = box(cx - half, cx + half, cy - width / 2, cy + width / 2, z0, z1)
    s = s.fuse(zcyl(width / 2, cx - half, cy, z0, z1)).fuse(zcyl(width / 2, cx + half, cy, z0, z1))

    return cq.Workplane("XY").polyline(points).close().extrude(z1 - z0).translate((0, 0, z0)).val()

    # Build in XY with (u, v) = (y, z), extrude along +Z by (x1 - x0), then map (u, v, t) -> (t, u, v).
    w = cq.Workplane("XY").polyline(points).close().extrude(x1 - x0).val()

    ref = {"bbox": [0, 0, 0, 10, 10, 10], "volume": 1000.0}
    same = {"bbox": [0, 0, 0, 10, 10, 10], "volume": 1000.0}
    assert forge_train.measurements_match(same, ref)  # 1e-6 prefilter hit

    assert matched and idx == 1
    matched, _ = forge_train.code_matches_exam(other, [ref])
    assert not matched

    calls = []
    def scorer(t, r):

        return False
    matched, _ = forge_train.code_matches_exam(same, [ref], scorer)
    assert not matched and len(calls) == 1
    matched, _ = forge_train.code_matches_exam(other, [ref], scorer)

+def text6(p):

+    for i in range(p["n"]):

+        lines.append(

+            % (i + 1, "up" if i % 2 == 0 else "down", num(v[0][0]),

+def src6(p):

+                 % (num(v[0][0]), num(v[0][1]), num(v[1][0]),

+# ------------------------------------------------------- 7. T-slot rail

+def gen7(rng):

+    W = r1(rng, 34, 46)
+    H = r1(rng, 24, 34)
+    wn = r1(rng, 8, 12)

+    sd = r1(rng, 12, 18)
+    uh = r1(rng, 5, 8)
+    return {"L": L, "W": W, "H": H, "wn": wn, "ww": ww, "sd": sd,
+            "uh": uh, "z0": round(H - sd, 1),
+            "z1": round(H - sd + uh, 1),
+            "x1": r1(rng, 10, 14),
+            "x2": round(L - rng.uniform(10, 14), 1),
+            "dh": r1(rng, 5, 8), "yc": 0.0}
+
+
+def text7(p):
+    yc = p["W"] / 2 + p["yc"]
+    return (
+        "Units: millimetres. Z is up. A T-slot rail: a bar X from 0 to "
+        "%s, Y from 0 to %s, Z from 0 to %s. A T-shaped slot runs along "
+        "X for the whole length, centred at Y = %s: a narrow opening %s "
+        "wide from the top face (Z = %s) down to Z = %s, and a wider "
+        "undercut %s wide from Z = %s down to the slot floor at Z = %s. "
+        "Two end holes of diameter %s go through along Z at (X, Y) = "
+        "(%s, %s) and (%s, %s)."
+        % (num(p["L"]), num(p["W"]), num(p["H"]), num(yc), num(p["wn"]),
+           num(p["H"]), num(p["z1"]), num(p["ww"]), num(p["z1"]),
+           num(p["z0"]), num(p["dh"]), num(p["x1"]), num(p["W"] / 2),
+           num(p["x2"]), num(p["W"] / 2)))

+def src7(p):
+    yc = p["W"] / 2 + p["yc"]

+           (yc + p["wn"] / 2, p["H"]), (yc - p["wn"] / 2, p["H"]),

+            "r": r, "td": td, "tw": tw, "thd": thd, "hx": 0.0}
+
+
+def _tabs8(p):
+    cx, cy = p["L"] / 2, p["W"] / 2
+    hw = p["tw"] / 2
+    return [
+        ("left", -p["td"], 3, cy - hw, cy + hw,
+         -p["td"] / 2 + p["hx"], cy),
+        ("right", p["L"] - 3, p["L"] + p["td"], cy - hw, cy + hw,

+def text8(p):

+def job_id(family, n):
+    """Job id: F<family>-<n>."""
+    return "F%d-%d" % (family, n)

+def generate_all(seed=SEED, per_family=JOBS_PER_FAMILY):
+    """Generate every job: [{id, family, text, reference}]. Deterministic
+    in seed: the same seed gives the same file."""
+    rng = random.Random(seed)
+    jobs = []
+    for family in range(1, N_FAMILIES + 1):
+        fam = FAMILIES[family]
+        for n in range(1, per_family + 1):
+            params = fam["gen"](rng)
+            jobs.append({
+                "id": job_id(family, n),
+                "family": family,
+                "text": fam["text"](params),
+                "reference": fam["src"](params),
+            })
+    return jobs

+def choose_dev_ids(jobs, seed=SEED, per_family=2):
+    """Seed-chosen dev split: 2 ids per family (20). Deterministic."""
+    rng = random.Random(seed)

+    for family in range(1, N_FAMILIES + 1):
+        ids = sorted(j["id"] for j in jobs if j["family"] == family)

+            params = FAMILIES[fam]["gen"](rng)
+            if fam == family:
